stem: How many interpenetrating hydrogel networks make up the architecture that reaches over 1000-fold linear expansion?
answer: Four networks
label: Abstract · architecture

stem: What three steps did the authors hypothesize would let individual protein residues be imaged separately?
choices: Anchor side chains, stain with heavy metals, image by electron microscopy
Cleave side chains, anchor backbones, sharpen the point spread function
Anchor side chains, cleave backbone bonds, expand residues apart
Anchor backbones, digest side chains, sequence the released residues
answer: Anchor side chains, cleave backbone bonds, expand residues apart
label: Abstract · premise

stem: What does the ~0.38 nm spacing between adjacent backbone alpha carbons become after 1000-fold linear expansion?
answer: About 380 nm
label: Introduction · why 1000×

stem: What went wrong with the five-network composite built from the original sodium acrylate/Bis gel alternating with neutral re-embedding?
choices: It dissolved during the second round of polymerization
It became dense and diffusion-restrictive, impeding staining
It expanded unevenly, distorting molecular distances
It failed to anchor peptide fragments after digestion
answer: It became dense and diffusion-restrictive, impeding staining
label: Results · why classic ExM failed

stem: What total expansion did the sodium acrylate/DMAA gel reach over five rounds alternating with neutral re-embedding?
answer: About 96×
label: Results · SA/DMAA gel

stem: Which change raised single-round expansion of the sodium acrylate/DMAA gel from about 10× to about 18×?
answer: Lowering the initiator concentration
label: Results · single-round gain

stem: How far did a cleavable DATD re-embedding scaffold push five-network expansion beyond the earlier 96×?
choices: To about 270×, and up to about 718×
To about 150×, and up to about 300×
To about 500×, and up to about 1500×
To about 44×, and up to about 52×
answer: To about 270×, and up to about 718×
label: Results · DATD scaffold

stem: Why did the authors abandon the cleavable DATD re-embedding scaffold despite its higher expansion?
choices: Periodate cleavage might damage the charged network too
The scaffold shrank too much during casting
The scaffold could not be polymerized reproducibly
The scaffold blocked fluorophore diffusion after expansion
answer: Periodate cleavage might damage the charged network too
label: Results · why drop DATD

stem: When a charged monomer solution was cast directly into an expanded charged gel, how far did the gel contract?
answer: From about 18× to about 10×
label: Results · ionic-in-ionic casting

stem: By roughly what fraction did each casting round contract the expanded gel in the four-network sequence?
answer: About 50%
label: Results · contraction per round

stem: What sequence of linear expansion factors did the four rounds of ionic-in-ionic casting produce?
label: Results · expansion sequence

stem: What brought the ~1500× four-network gel down to the ~1000× state used for imaging?
choices: A fifth round of neutral re-embedding
answer: Equilibration in phosphate buffered saline
label: Results · stabilization step

stem: What median linear expansion did the modified protocol with two monomer incubations per round reach?
answer: About 1900×
label: Results · beyond 1000×

stem: How far apart were the two fluorophores on the site-directed nanobody used as a nanoruler?
answer: About 4 nm
label: Results · nanobody ruler

stem: Why were the low-expansion nanobody gels imaged with ONE microscopy rather than a conventional confocal?
choices: At 18× the gel was too dense for confocal objectives
At 18× the fluorophores were too dim for confocal detectors
At 18× the 4 nm gap is still about 72 nm, below the diffraction limit
At 18× the gel could not be mounted on a coverslip
answer: At 18× the 4 nm gap is still about 72 nm, below the diffraction limit
label: Results · why ONE at low factors

stem: After normalizing by expansion factor, what biological separation did the nanobody fluorophore measurements infer?
choices: About 1 nm, below the expected labeling distance
About 10 nm, above the expected labeling distance
About 4 nm, matching the expected labeling distance
A value that drifted upward with expansion factor
answer: About 4 nm, matching the expected labeling distance
label: Results · proportional scaling

stem: What did the authors blame for nanobody distance measurements larger than the protein itself?
choices: Anisotropic swelling stretching the gel along one axis
One fluorophore lost, so the nearest neighbour sat on another nanobody
Chromatic aberration between the two detection channels
answer: One fluorophore lost, so the nearest neighbour sat on another nanobody
label: Results · outlier explanation

stem: How was the nanobody represented in the model that predicted the measured distance distribution?
choices: A full atomic structure from the crystallographic coordinates
A rigid globule with fluorophores on flexible linkers
A molecular dynamics ensemble of backbone conformations
A flexible chain with fluorophores fixed to its ends
answer: A rigid globule with fluorophores on flexible linkers
label: Results · nanobody model

stem: How did fluorescein peak positions in averaged mCLING images compare with molecular dynamics predictions?
choices: They matched at both low and high expansion
They matched only at high expansion
They matched only at low expansion
They matched in spacing but not in peak count
answer: They matched at both low and high expansion
label: Results · mCLING peaks vs model

stem: What coefficient of determination described agreement between measured and modelled numbers of fluorescein spots?
label: Results · model agreement

stem: How did measured mCLING peak-to-peak distances compare statistically with the modelled distances?
answer: Statistically indistinguishable from the model
label: Results · distance agreement

stem: What analysis was needed to read amino-acid-level positions out of the mCLING images?
choices: Simple two-dimensional averaging of aligned signals
Super-resolution fluctuation analysis over thousands of frames
Deconvolution against a measured point spread function
answer: Simple two-dimensional averaging of aligned signals
label: Results · analysis needed

stem: What signal combination defined a putative mCLING peptide in the three-dimensional data?
choices: One Atto647N dye with at least two fluorescein dyes
One Atto647N dye with at least four fluorescein dyes
At least four Atto647N dyes with one fluorescein dye
One Atto647N dye with exactly five fluorescein dyes
answer: One Atto647N dye with at least four fluorescein dyes
label: Results · putative peptide

stem: What dominant conformation did molecular dynamics give the mCLING peptide, and what drove it?
choices: An extended rod, driven by charge repulsion
A compact globule, driven by its lysine residues
A curved C-shape, driven by its palmitoyl tail
A helical turn, driven by backbone hydrogen bonding
answer: A curved C-shape, driven by its palmitoyl tail
label: Results · mCLING shape

stem: How many putative peptides came out of the 27,426 Atto647N localizations?
answer: 6,284 peptides
label: Results · peptide yield

stem: Beyond roughly how many modelled conformations did the per-molecule RMSD estimates stop changing?
answer: About 600 conformations
label: Results · ensemble size

stem: What mean deviation did measured dye coordinates show from their best-matching modelled peptide conformations?
answer: About 0.57 nm
label: Results · RMSD

stem: What did comparable per-axis RMSD values in x, y and z establish about 1000-fold expansion?
choices: It is anisotropic along the optical axis
It compresses molecules along one axis during casting
It is isotropic only below 100-fold expansion
It is isotropic at the single-molecule level
answer: It is isotropic at the single-molecule level
label: Results · isotropy

stem: What expansion factor did fitting a scale to individual peptides return, against the bulk gel measurement?
answer: About 1056×
label: Results · single-molecule factor

stem: What units did the modelled nanometre-scale nearest-neighbour dye distances appear in after ~1000× expansion?
choices: Nanometres, at a thousand times the numeric values
Micrometres, at a thousand times the numeric values
Millimetres, at nearly the same numeric values
Micrometres, at nearly the same numeric values
answer: Micrometres, at nearly the same numeric values
label: Results · kNN distances

stem: How did the Kolmogorov–Smirnov D statistic against randomized emitter placement behave from the first to the fifth nearest neighbour?
choices: It fell, so larger clusters were more random
It rose, so larger clusters were less random
It stayed flat across all five ranks
It rose only for the dye pairs of different colours
answer: It rose, so larger clusters were less random
label: Results · versus random

stem: What resolution did Fourier shell correlation give for the GFP reconstruction at 100× expansion with ONE microscopy?
label: Results · GFP resolution

stem: What does expansion microscopy record that electron microscopy does not restrict itself to?
choices: Only the positions of backbone alpha carbons
Only the positions of anchored residues
Only the positions of surface-exposed atoms
Only the positions of charged side chains
answer: Only the positions of anchored residues
label: Results · what ExM reports

stem: What range of separations can neighbouring anchored lysine side chains span, setting the sampling limit?
answer: About 0.44 to 1.41 nm
label: Results · sampling limit

stem: What imposes the roughly 10 Å upper bound that the GFP reconstruction approaches?
choices: The numerical aperture of the objective
Amino acid spacing, not atomic spacing
The point spread function of ONE microscopy
The pixel size of the confocal detector
answer: Amino acid spacing, not atomic spacing
label: Results · approaching the limit

stem: In the single-colour lysine scheme, where does the fluorescence from a digested fragment appear?
choices: At the newly exposed N terminus of the fragment
Spread evenly along the anchored fragment
At the original lysine anchoring coordinate
At the centroid of the parent protein
answer: At the original lysine anchoring coordinate
label: Results · single-colour limit

stem: What kind of reagent did the authors say residue-resolved multicolour mapping would require?
choices: A trivalent molecule binding one residue, the gel and a dye
An antibody raised against each residue class
A cleavable linker releasing dyes after expansion
A second gel network cast around each fragment
answer: A trivalent molecule binding one residue, the gel and a dye
label: Results · what multicolour needs

stem: How many human proteins entered the simulation of identifiability from residue coordinates?
answer: 23,391 proteins
label: Results · simulation scale

stem: What did the 5 Å and 10 Å distortion levels in the identifiability simulation represent?
choices: The best and worst single molecules measured
The lateral and axial resolution of the confocal
Typical measured performance and a conservative case
Distortion before and after salt stabilization
answer: Typical measured performance and a conservative case
label: Results · distortion levels

stem: What criterion counted a simulated protein as uniquely identifiable from its residue coordinates?
choices: Its match scored below a fixed RMSD threshold
Its nearest match was its own undistorted structure
It matched its own structure in at least half of trials
No other protein matched it within one standard deviation
answer: Its nearest match was its own undistorted structure
label: Results · identifiability criterion

stem: What share of the human proteome was identifiable from surface lysines alone at 5 Å distortion?
answer: About 89 to 93%
label: Results · one label class

stem: Which residue class was added to lysine as the second colour in the identifiability simulation?
answer: Cysteine
label: Results · two label classes

stem: How many chemically addressable residue classes did the simulation suggest would identify over 99% of the proteome?
answer: Three classes
label: Results · three classes suffice

stem: What linear expansion do established iterative methods such as iExM and pan-ExM typically reach?
answer: About 16 to 25×
label: Discussion · prior art

stem: Which mechanism did the authors offer first for how structure survives 1000-fold swelling?
choices: Bond scission then reincorporation into later networks
Progressive crosslinking of the earliest network
Displacement of water by the charged monomer
Covalent exchange between the dye and the gel
answer: Bond scission then reincorporation into later networks
label: Discussion · proposed mechanism

stem: How much did the expansion factor of a mounted gel drift over 98 hours at room temperature?
answer: About 0.3%
label: Discussion · gel stability

stem: At 1000-fold linear expansion, what does a 10 µm cell become?
choices: About 10 µm, the size of an unexpanded cell
About 10 mm, the size of a mouse brain
About 1 mm, the size of a tissue section
About 10 cm, the size of a rat brain
answer: About 10 mm, the size of a mouse brain
label: Discussion · imaging burden

stem: What sets the roughly 10 Å floor on reconstruction precision in 1000ExM?
choices: Shot noise in the confocal detector
Residual anisotropy in the fourth gel network
Side chain length and rotational freedom at anchoring
answer: Side chain length and rotational freedom at anchoring
label: Discussion · precision floor
